newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African mining group sold to black investors.
newsitem.headline: S.African mining group sold to black investors.

text.p: In another sign of change in post-apartheid South Africa, the nation's biggest company said Tuesday it agreed to sell a piece of a major mining subsidiary to black investors in a $630 million deal.

The agreement by Anglo American Corp. to sell its 34.9 percent stake in JCI Ltd. to African Mining Consortium and an investment firm puts one of the gems of the nation's mining industry in black hands.

The JCI sale is the second major sale of assets by Anglo American to black interests. It recently sold off its 35 percent stake in Johnnies Industrial Corp. Ltd. -- an industrial holding concern -- to the National Empowerment Consortium.
"The main thrust in these cases is to make our contribution to black empowerment," Anglo Chairman Julian Ogilvie Thompson said when he announced the JCI deal.
The JCI and Johnnies deals give blacks control or influence over companies representing nearly one-tenth of the stock market value on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
Anglo said it had no plans to sell off other assets similar in size to the Johnnies and JCI stakes being sold.
African Mining Consortium is paying 54.50 rand ($12) a share for the JCI stake, with payment due at the end of February, an 11 percent premium to JCI's closing stock price Tuesday.
As in the Johnnies deal, Anglo will retain an interest, holding some 12 percent of JCI.
The deal is also a major coup for Capital Alliance, the investment firm that last month hired Mark Barnes, a former top official at Standard Corporate and Merchant Bank, as its chief executive.

Ogilvie Thompson said it was unlikely Anglo would take the $458 million from the Johnnies sale or the $630 million from the JCI sale out of South Africa due to the country's current stringent foreign exchange control regulations.
Instead, he said the group was likely to invest its new income in projects within South Africa.
